correctness.rationale: Every allowed binary digit pair is (0,0),(1,0),(0,1), so the cyclic Fourier coefficient factors over j as ∏(1+ζ^(2^j u)+ζ^(2^j v)). For a power-of-two M, any two Mth roots z,w satisfy |1+z+w|≥||1+z|−1|=|2cos(πt)−1|≥3|t−1/3|≥1/M; the concavity/chord and tangent estimates cover t∈[0,1/2], and 3∤M ensures separation. Thus σ_n≥2^{−n(n+1)/2}. The explicit conjugate frequencies u_n=(2^n−(−1)^n)/3,v_n=−u_n modulo 2^n are simultaneously within 1/(3·2^(n−j)) of primitive cube-root cancellation at each digit scale; Lipschitz bound 4π gives σ_n≤(4π/3)^n2^{−n(n+1)/2}. Triangle inequality makes max multiplier 3^n, so κ=3^n/σ and log2 κ/n²→1/2. Does not prove exact finite minimizers.
